modification_description: Campaign baseline at latent_dim=60, full budget (n_epochs=200) — HP reset to neutral/near-zero values (lr=1e-5, weight_decay=0, dropout_rate=0, noise_std=0, patience=30) rather than carried from the dim=240 champion, since a 4x smaller bottleneck likely needs a different regularization/lr operating point
Raise lr 10x (1e-5 -> 1e-4) after the baseline's scheduler decayed lr 4x before patience expired, suggesting 1e-5 was too conservative for this bottleneck size
Push lr further (1e-4 -> 3e-4) after the previous trial's clean win, to test whether the improving trend continues or 1e-4 was already near the local optimum
Push lr further (3e-4 -> 6e-4), close to the dim=240 champion's 8e-4, since the last two lr increases both won with diminishing but still-positive gains and no instability yet
Last lr step (6e-4 -> 8e-4), matching the dim=240 champion exactly, to close the lr axis given sharply diminishing gains and the first visible raw-lr noise at 6e-4
Switch axis to dropout (0.0 -> 0.05) on top of the champion's lr=6e-4, testing the dim=240 champion's dropout value now that the lr axis is closed
Test a small weight_decay (0.0 -> 1e-6) on top of the champion's lr=6e-4, a gentler/smoother regularizer than the dropout that just FAILED
Test small input-space denoising (noise_std 0.0 -> 0.0001) on top of the champion's lr=6e-4, the one regularization mechanism not yet tried (dropout and weight_decay both failed)
Push noise_std further (0.0001 -> 0.0003) after the small win, to test whether the denoising axis has more headroom before approaching the magnitude that caused catastrophic failure at dim=240
Map the noise_std cliff boundary — test 0.0002 (between the winning 0.0001 and the badly-failing 0.0003) on top of the champion's lr=6e-4
Test patience increase (30 -> 45) on top of the champion, the last opened HP not yet touched, to check whether more room after the plateau ever finds a better epoch
Push patience further (45 -> 60) after the last trial's win, now understanding the real lever is the coupled patience_scheduler=patience//5 stretching the whole LR decay schedule
Push patience further (60 -> 90) to test whether the schedule-stretching effect finally reverses, given the last step's shrinking gain and widening train/val gap
Map the patience boundary — test 75 (patience_scheduler=15, between the winning 60/12 and the failing 90/18) to refine the practical optimum of the schedule-length axis
Interaction check — retest lr=8e-4 (which FAILED under patience=30/patience_scheduler=6) now under the champion's patience=60/patience_scheduler=12, to see if the longer schedule changes the outcome
Interaction re-check — retest dropout=0.05 (FAILED under patience=30 with a tight train/val gap of 0.045) now under the champion's patience=60, where the gap has widened back to 0.080
Ablation — remove noise_std (0.0001 -> 0.0) from the champion under patience=60, to check whether its small individual win (found under patience=30) still holds at the much longer schedule
Interaction re-check — retest weight_decay=1e-6 (near-neutral under patience=30) now under the champion's patience=60, completing the regularizer-under-new-schedule sweep
Control replicate #1 — exact champion config (lr=6e-4, noise_std=0.0001, patience=60), no HP change, to measure run-to-run variance under batch_size=1 despite the fixed seed
Control replicate #2 — exact champion config again, to get a 3-point sample (0.8148, 0.8050, ?) of run-to-run variance at this operating point
Control replicate #3 — exact champion config again, given the surprisingly wide spread (0.8148/0.8050/0.7396) seen in the first two replicates, to firm up the variance estimate with a 4-point sample

Map the noise_std axis below its current value — test 0.00005 (half of the champion's 0.0001), the one point on this axis never tried, now interpreting the result against the ~0.03 noise floor just established
